result:
I've completed the DG1 round-3 code-security review. **My verdict is FAIL** for frozen candidate `f0baa87d…95a8` (source commit `5204179`; HEAD `4f486b9` adds only metadata). The recomputed candidate ID matched in the real tree at the start and end of my run, and in a disposable clone.

The main reason is a new High finding in the redesigned dependency installer. Three of the fixes I was asked to verify also don't hold up.

### Findings that verified (closable)
| Finding | What I saw |
|---|---|
| F-DG1-102 | The installer clears the environment (no host secrets reach it), drops all capabilities (CapEff 0) and mounts the repo read-only. All 19 checks from the round-2 escape script were refused. |
| F-DG1-115 | The implementer's race tests A–D passed in 3 runs. My own interleaving E (the revoke commits between the create's authorization and its derive step) returned 403, rolled back and wrote the audit event. In F (45 concurrent create/revoke rounds) no derived assignment survived its revoked source. |
| F-DG1-117 | All five reported loader forms are now caught. A planted module file makes `architecture.test.ts` fail; removing it restores 46/46. |
| F-DG1-116 | All 11 round-2 and assignment bypass routes are rejected; the deploy-script tests pass 48/48. |
| F-DG1-108 / F-DG1-203 | Node, postgres and playwright are pinned by digest everywhere. Keycloak is the only unpinned image and carries a `blockedReason`. Pin-images tests pass 13/13. |
| F-DG1-106 | The round-1 repro now gives create 201, then read-back 200 (was 404). |
| F-DG1-112 | Production refuses a non-loopback http `APP_BASE_URL` at startup (exit 78). |
| F-DG1-202 | The assembled runtime tree includes design-tokens and starts the API: `/healthz` and `/readyz` both return 200. |

### Findings that did not verify (still open)
- **F-DG1-113 and F-DG1-114:** the round-2 routes are closed, but the outcome these findings require still fails because of F-DG1-118 below.
- **F-DG1-107:** the CI checker deliberately allows `success()` in a job's `if:`. Under GitHub's rules, `if: success() || true` or `!success()` lets a product job run after the delivery-gates job failed. All three variants I tried pass the checker. This is based on GitHub's documented behaviour; I could not run it on GitHub.

### New findings
- **F-DG1-118 (High, mandatory, REQ-DLV-042):** after an install, `install-sandbox.sh` (lines 142–148) copies back every directory named `node_modules` from the throwaway copy, at the same path in the real repo.
  - An allow-listed package's install script can therefore plant files under `.claude/rules`, `skills`, `commands` and `agents`, inside `.git/hooks`, `tools/gates`, `docs/delivery` and `.vscode/`. `git status` doesn't show them because `node_modules/` is git-ignored.
  - A directory name containing a newline made the installer delete a directory outside the repo root. The installer still exits 0 because copy errors are ignored.
  - The installer's own tests (AC-7/AC-8) only cover the `run` mode, so they miss this. They also delete a developer's existing `.vscode` or `CLAUDE.local.md` in the real repo during cleanup.
  - The allow-list is empty today, so nothing exploits this yet. The flaw is in the very control meant to contain an allow-listed package.
- **F-DG1-119 (Medium):** CI cannot go green. The `verify` job runs `pnpm format:check` (ci.yml:62), and it fails on the committed `deploy/images.lock.json`, which `pin-images.mjs:145` writes in a non-Prettier format. Every later job depends on `verify`.
- **F-DG1-120 (Low):** the CI checker doesn't restrict the inputs of the delivery-gates checkout step. `ref:` or `repository:` would let the gate validate a different tree than the one the product jobs build.
- **F-DG1-121 (Low):** the module-boundary lint misses four aliased forms of `.constructor`. I confirmed in Node 22 that one of them really loads another module's file.

### Checks I couldn't run fully
- The installer test suite: 11 of 12 cases passed, including AC-7/AC-8. The remaining case (AC-1, create populates `node_modules`) needs the npm registry, which this sandbox can't reach. I shared the evidence for that behaviour from my own installs.
- `pnpm deps:verify` also needs the registry; it wasn't in my assigned list.
- The container image itself wasn't built (no Docker access); I tested the identical assembled runtime tree instead.

### Other checks
- `typecheck`, `build`, `lint`, `openapi:lint` (33 operations) and `check:no-cdn` all passed.
- Unit tests passed 235/235.
- The integration suite passed 197/197 on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 database (port 5471).
- Gate and agent tool tests passed 105/105.
- `validate.mjs --stage DG0 --historical` passed.

### Assigned requirements
- **Not met:** REQ-DLV-042 (F-DG1-118), REQ-DLV-025 (F-DG1-107 open, plus F-DG1-120) and REQ-DLV-033 (CI cannot pass, F-DG1-119).
- **Met:** REQ-S16-001, REQ-S16-004, REQ-S19-004 and REQ-S19-006. REQ-S16-003 is met, with the Low F-DG1-121 still open.

During my run, the other reviewers' round-3 records were auto-committed to the real repo. They don't change the candidate ID, and I didn't open them. Disposable clones and scratch databases were removed.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-3/`:
- `code-security-reviewer.json` (record; validates against the review schema)
- `code-security-reviewer.findings.json` (validates against the findings schema)
- `code-security-reviewer.verifications.json`

Evidence and reproductions are in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/code-security/round-3/`.
